pharm-gi:gimap.q: Which receptor do ondansetron and granisetron block?
pharm-gi:gimap.e: Central and peripheral 5-HT₃ antagonism prevents emesis.

o: Binding the ulcer base as a protective barrier
Blocking H₂ receptors on parietal cells
pharm-gi:gimap.e: Needs acid to polymerize; avoid with PPIs.

pharm-gi:gimap.q: A 55-year-old man receiving cisplatin is given an IV antiemetic before each cycle. He later reports headache and constipation, and his QTc is 500 ms. Which receptor does this drug block?
pharm-gi:gimap.e: Ondansetron (5-HT₃ antagonist) causes headache, constipation and QT prolongation. NK₁ antagonists (aprepitant) are added for delayed emesis.

pharm-gi:acid.e: Gynecomastia, impotence; crosses BBB and placenta.
Proton pumps are activated by meals.

pharm-gi:acid.q: A 61-year-old man on stable warfarin buys an over-the-counter drug for heartburn. Four weeks later his INR has risen from 2.4 to 4.6 and he has tender breast enlargement. Which drug did he most likely start?
pharm-gi:acid.e: Cimetidine inhibits CYP450 (↑ warfarin) and has antiandrogen effects causing gynecomastia. Famotidine has neither effect to a meaningful degree.

pharm-gi:mucosal.e: Aluminum hydroxide constipates; calcium carbonate can cause hypercalcemia.
Uterine contraction; also used for medical abortion and labor induction.

pharm-gi:mucosal.q: A 64-year-old man with a benign gastric ulcer is prescribed a drug that forms a viscous gel adhering to the ulcer base. Which concurrently prescribed drug would most reduce its effectiveness?
pharm-gi:mucosal.e: Sucralfate needs an acidic pH to polymerize, so acid suppression with a PPI reduces its effect. Amoxicillin does not alter gastric pH.

pharm-gi:octreotide.e: Used for variceal bleeding, acromegaly, carcinoid and VIPoma.

pharm-gi:octreotide.q: A long-term adverse effect of octreotide:

A 58-year-old man has episodic facial flushing, watery diarrhea and wheezing. Echocardiography shows tricuspid regurgitation, urinary 5-HIAA is elevated and CT shows multiple liver metastases. Which drug is best for controlling his symptoms?
pharm-gi:octreotide.e: Carcinoid syndrome is controlled with a somatostatin analog, which inhibits release of serotonin and other tumor hormones. Loperamide treats diarrhea only, not flushing.

pharm-gi:ibd.q: Sulfasalazine is cleaved by colonic bacteria into:
pharm-gi:ibd.e: Sulfapyridine causes oligospermia and sulfa toxicity.

pharm-gi:ibd.q: For moderate–severe Crohn disease, which biologic is used?
pharm-gi:ibd.e: Anti-TNF; screen for latent TB first.

pharm-gi:ibd.q: A 29-year-old man with fistulizing Crohn disease is about to start infliximab. He was born in a country with high tuberculosis prevalence. Which test should be done before the first dose?
pharm-gi:ibd.e: TNF-α blockade can reactivate latent TB, so screen with IGRA or tuberculin skin test. TPMT activity is checked before azathioprine/6-MP.

pharm-gi:antidiar.e: Poor CNS penetration; low addictive potential; slows intestinal motility.

pharm-gi:antidiar.q: Antimotility agents should be avoided in:
pharm-gi:antidiar.e: Risk of toxic megacolon or HUS. Examples: C. difficile, Shiga toxin–producing E. coli.

pharm-gi:antidiar.q: A 32-year-old woman with diarrhea-predominant IBS uses an over-the-counter μ-opioid agonist that slows gut transit. At usual doses she has no sedation or euphoria. Which property best explains the lack of CNS effects?
pharm-gi:antidiar.e: Loperamide is pumped out of the CNS by P-glycoprotein, so effects stay peripheral. It is a μ (not κ) agonist.

pharm-gi:antiemetic.e: Used for gastroparesis; causes EPS and tardive dyskinesia.
Added for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting.

pharm-gi:antiemetic.q: A 47-year-old woman with diabetic gastroparesis has taken a prokinetic drug for 5 months. She now has involuntary lip-smacking and tongue-thrusting movements. Blockade at which site explains this effect?
o: D₂ receptors in the nigrostriatal tract
M₁ receptors in the basal ganglia
H₁ receptors in the vomiting center
pharm-gi:antiemetic.e: Metoclopramide blocks D₂ receptors, causing tardive dyskinesia with long use (limit to ≤ 12 weeks). 5-HT₄ agonism is a prokinetic mechanism, not a cause of dyskinesia.

pharm-gi:laxative.q: Lactulose is used in hepatic encephalopathy because it:
o: Is converted by gut flora to acids that trap NH₄⁺
Acts as a stimulant laxative like senna
pharm-gi:laxative.e: Osmotic laxative; rifaximin is often added.
Peripheral μ antagonist that does not cross the BBB.

pharm-gi:laxative.q: A 56-year-old man with cirrhosis becomes confused 2 days after a variceal bleed. He has asterixis and plasma ammonia 140 µmol/L. Which mechanism underlies the first-line drug for his condition?
pharm-gi:laxative.e: Lactulose is metabolized by colonic bacteria to acids that convert NH₃ to non-absorbable NH₄⁺ and act as an osmotic laxative. It does not act on hepatic ammonia metabolism.

o: Agonizing GLP-1 receptors to slow emptying

pharm-gi:orlistat.q: A GLP-1 agonist approved for weight loss:
pharm-gi:orlistat.e: Liraglutide and semaglutide; GI side effects.

pharm-gi:orlistat.q: A 38-year-old woman with obesity began a weight-loss drug 6 months ago and reports oily stools and fecal urgency after fatty meals. She now has difficulty seeing in dim light. Which supplement should have been advised?
o: Vitamins A, D, E and K
pharm-gi:orlistat.e: Orlistat inhibits gastric and pancreatic lipase, causing steatorrhea and fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption (vitamin A → night blindness). B12 absorption is unaffected.

pharm-gi:pud.e: Gastrinoma causes refractory ulcers; resect if possible.

pharm-gi:pud.q: First-line therapy for GERD with erosive esophagitis:
pharm-gi:pud.e: PPIs heal esophagitis better than H₂ blockers.

pharm-gi:pud.q: A 71-year-old woman with severe knee osteoarthritis must continue daily naproxen. She had a bleeding gastric ulcer last year; H. pylori testing is negative. Which strategy best reduces her risk of recurrent ulcer?
o: Add an antacid after each meal
Add a daily proton pump inhibitor
pharm-gi:pud.e: PPIs (or misoprostol) effectively prevent NSAID-induced ulcers. Standard-dose H₂ blockers prevent duodenal but not gastric NSAID ulcers.

pharm-gi:cirrhosis.q: Nonselective β-blocker used to prevent variceal bleeding:
Diuretic of choice for cirrhotic ascites:
A 57-year-old man with cirrhosis has medium-sized esophageal varices without prior bleeding and is started on propranolol rather than metoprolol. Which effect of β₂ blockade explains this choice?
o: Direct relaxation of hepatic stellate cells
pharm-gi:cirrhosis.e: Nonselective β-blockers lower cardiac output (β₁) and, via β₂ blockade, allow unopposed α₁ splanchnic vasoconstriction, reducing portal inflow. They do not affect ammonia clearance.

title.th: เคสใหญ่: ปวดลิ้นปี่ถ่ายดำ
title.en: Boss case: Epigastric pain and black stools

boss.case: A 52-year-old man with knee osteoarthritis takes naproxen daily. He has 2 months of burning epigastric pain that improves with meals, and 2 days of black tarry stools. Endoscopy: duodenal ulcer; biopsy urease test positive.

qs.q: Two main causes of his ulcer:
qs.e: Both are the commonest causes of PUD.

qs.q: First-line H. pylori regimen (where clarithromycin resistance is high):
qs.e: Clarithromycin triple therapy only where resistance is low. Quadruple = PPI + bismuth + metronidazole + tetracycline.

o: Coating the ulcer base in acid
qs.e: Omeprazole and others are activated in the acidic canaliculus of the parietal cell.

qs.q: Which drug prevents NSAID-induced ulcers by replacing prostaglandins?
Long-term PPI use is associated with:
qs.e: Also ↓ B12 absorption and fractures. Cimetidine (H₂ blocker) is the one that causes gynecomastia.

title.th: ถ่ายเป็นเลือดปนมูก

stem.th: หญิง 28 ปี ถ่ายเป็นเลือดปนมูกวันละ 5 ครั้ง ปวดเบ่ง มา 6 สัปดาห์
stem.en: A 28-year-old woman has 6 weeks of bloody, mucoid diarrhea 5 times a day with tenesmus.

info.th: Colonoscopy: continuous inflammation จาก rectum
info.en: Colonoscopy: continuous inflammation from the rectum

steps.q: Loperamide should be avoided now because:
o: It is ineffective in all diarrhea
Risk of toxic megacolon in active colitis
steps.e: Antimotility agents in severe colitis are dangerous.
Vedolizumab (anti-α4β7 integrin) is an alternative. Screen for latent TB and HBV first.

info.th: ต่อมาอาการรุนแรง ไม่ตอบสนอง steroid
info.en: Later she has a severe flare unresponsive to steroids

steps.q: Her husband, who also has ulcerative colitis, is on sulfasalazine. As they plan a pregnancy, the concern for him is:
steps.e: The sulfapyridine moiety causes reversible oligospermia (mesalamine does not). For her, sulfasalazine is acceptable in pregnancy with folate.
